title: Rare Coins
statementMd:
There are 𝑛n bags numbered from 11 to 𝑛n, the 𝑖i-th bag contains 𝑎𝑖ai golden coins and 𝑏𝑖bi silver coins.

The value of a gold coin is 11. The value of a silver coin is either 00 or 11, determined for each silver coin independently (00 with probability 1212, 11 with probability 1212).

You have to answer 𝑞q independent queries. Each query is the following:

- 𝑙l 𝑟r — calculate the probability that the total value of coins in bags from 𝑙l to 𝑟r is strictly greater than the total value in all other bags.

## Input

The first line contains two integers 𝑛n and 𝑞q (1≤𝑛,𝑞≤3⋅1051≤n,q≤3⋅105) — the number of bags and the number of queries, respectively.

The second line contains 𝑛n integers 𝑎1,𝑎2,…,𝑎𝑛a1,a2,…,an (0≤𝑎𝑖≤1060≤ai≤106) — the number of gold coins in the 𝑖i-th bag.

The third line contains 𝑛n integers 𝑏1,𝑏2,…,𝑏𝑛b1,b2,…,bn (0≤𝑏𝑖≤1060≤bi≤106) — the number of silver coins in the 𝑖i-th bag.

Next 𝑞q lines contain queries. The 𝑗j-th of the next 𝑞q lines contains two integers 𝑙𝑗lj and 𝑟𝑗rj (1≤𝑙𝑗≤𝑟𝑗≤𝑛1≤lj≤rj≤n) — the description of the 𝑗j-th query.

Additional constraints on the input:

- the sum of the array 𝑎a doesn't exceed 106106;
- the sum of the array 𝑏b doesn't exceed 106106.

## Output

For each query, print one integer — the probability that the total value of coins in bags from 𝑙l to 𝑟r is strictly greater than the total value in all other bags, taken modulo 998244353998244353.

Formally, the probability can be expressed as an irreducible fraction 𝑥𝑦xy. You have to print the value of 𝑥⋅𝑦−1mod998244353x⋅y−1mod998244353, where 𝑦−1y−1 is an integer such that 𝑦⋅𝑦−1mod998244353=1y⋅y−1mod998244353=1.

## Note

In both queries from the first example, the answer is 1414.
